hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Malaysia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Malaysia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Kuala Lumpur?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Malaysia is Kuala Lumpur.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Malaysia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malaysia article.

questions.proof: Kuala Lumpur is the national capital, largest city and the seat of the legislative branch of the federal government.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Malaysia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Malaysia is the Malaysian ringgit.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Malaysia about 330,803 square kilometres; North Korea about 120,540 square kilometres; Bhutan about 38,394 square kilometres; East Timor about 14,919 square kilometres.
